dataset_metadata.disclaimer: New AI-generated English drafts of the recorded Classical Chinese; not scholarly reviewed. Original source interpretations are not verified geometry or modern etymology.

shuowen:4201.text: Evening. Formed from 日, with 免 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4202.text: The sun darkening. Formed from 日 and abbreviated 氐; 氐 means below. Another explanation: 民 indicates the sound.

shuowen:4203.text: The time of dawn or dusk; the wording 日旦昏時 is uncertain. Formed from 日, with 䜌 indicating the sound. Read like 䜌 in 新城䜌中.

shuowen:4204.text: Not bright. Formed from 日, with 奄 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4205.text: The sun without light. Formed from 日, with 音 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4206.text: The end of the lunar month. Formed from 日, with 每 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4207.text: 埃𣉘, the sun without light. Formed from 日, with 能 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4208.text: Overcast and windy. Formed from 日, with 壹 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “Wind all day, and overcast.”

shuowen:4209.text: No rain. Formed from 日, with 干 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4210.text: Distant things merging in the view. Formed from 日 and 匕; 匕 means joining. Read like 窈 in 窈窕.

shuowen:4211.text: A stellar mansion of the White Tiger. Formed from 日, with 卯 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4212.text: Not long ago. Formed from 日, with 鄉 indicating the sound. The Spring and Autumn Commentary says: “In the third month of the earlier campaign.”

shuowen:4213.text: Previously, 曏. Formed from 日, with 襄 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4214.text: Accumulated days. Formed from 日, with 乍 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4215.text: Leisure. Formed from 日, with 叚 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4216.text: Not lasting long. Formed from 日, with 斬 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4217.text: A joyful appearance. Formed from 日, with 弁 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4218.text: Fine words. Formed from 日 and 曰. Another explanation: sunlight. The Odes says: “The east is bright.”

shuowen:4219.text: Beautiful light. Formed from 日, with 往 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4220.text: Great. Formed from 日, with 反 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4221.text: The next day. Formed from 日, with 立 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4222.text: Warm and damp. Formed from 日, with abbreviated 赧 indicating the sound. Pronounced the same as 赧.

shuowen:4223.text: Injured by summer heat. Formed from 日, with 曷 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4224.text: Hot. Formed from 日, with 者 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4225.text: 安㬮, warm. Formed from 日, with 難 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4226.text: Many tiny ends. Formed from looking at silk in sunlight. The ancient script uses it for 顯. Some explain it as many mouths. Read like 唫唫. Some take it as 繭, a cocoon: small cocoons occur here and there within silk floss.

shuowen:4227.text: To dry in the sun. Formed from 日, 出, 𠬞 and 米.

shuowen:4228.text: To expose to the sun. Formed from 日, with 麗 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4229.text: To dry. Plowing and exposing a field to the sun is 暵. Formed from 日, with 堇 indicating the sound. The Changes says: “For drying all things, nothing exceeds Li.”

shuowen:4230.text: To dry. Formed from 日, with 希 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4231.text: Dried meat. Formed from pieces of meat, with 日 drying them. It uses the same principle as 俎.

shuowen:4232.text: To grow closer daily. Formed from 日, with 匿 indicating the sound. The Spring and Autumn Commentary says: “Privately descending to intimate feasts”; the quoted phrase 私降暱燕 is uncertain.

shuowen:4233.text: Daily familiarity leading to mutual disrespect. Formed from 日, with 執 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4234.text: Not visible. Formed from 日, with abbreviated 否 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4235.text: The same or together. Formed from 日 and 比.

shuowen:4236.text: To encompass together. Formed from 日, with 亥 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4237.text: The sun without color. Formed from 日 and 並.

shuowen:4238.text: Bright. Formed from 日, with 堯 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4239.text: Dawn light, when the sun is about to rise. Formed from 日, with 斤 indicating the sound. Read like 希.

shuowen:4240.text: 曈曨, when the sun is about to brighten. Formed from 日, with 童 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4241.text: 曈曨, the light before sunrise. Formed from 日, with 龍 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4242.text: Bright. Formed from 日, with 戶 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4243.text: Bright. Formed from 日, with 方 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4244.text: Bright. Formed from 日, with 夋 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4245.text: Bright. Formed from 日, with 成 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4246.text: A long day. Formed from 日 and 永, combining their meanings.

shuowen:4247.text: Vapor around the sun or moon. Formed from 日, with 軍 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4248.text: A complete year. Formed from 日 and 卒; 卒 also indicates the sound.

shuowen:4249.text: Bright; concealed. Formed from 日, with 央 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4250.text: Dawn. Formed from 日, with 署 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4251.text: The sun slanting westward, 𣅦. Formed from 日, with 失 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4252.text: Clouds spreading. Formed from 日 and 雲, combining their meanings.

shuowen:4253.text: To calculate the celestial phenomena. Formed from 日, with 厤 indicating the sound. The Records of the Historian also uses 歷.

shuowen:4254.text: To raise. Formed from 日, with 卬 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4255.text: The sun rising. Formed from 日, with 升 indicating the sound. Ancient writing used only 升.

shuowen:4256.text: Bright. Formed from 日 appearing above 一; 一 is the ground. All characters in this group are formed from 旦.

shuowen:4257.text: The sun partly visible. Formed from 旦, with 旣 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4258.text: The sun first rising, its light 倝倝. Formed from 旦, with 㫃 indicating the sound. All characters in this group are formed from 倝.

shuowen:4260.text: Dawn. Formed from 倝, with 舟 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4261.text: A banner’s streamers, fluttering and trailing, 㫃蹇. Formed from 屮, bent downward, with hanging streamers passing in and out. Read like 偃. An ancient man named 㫃 had the courtesy name Ziyou. All characters in the 㫃人 group follow 㫃.

shuowen:4262.text: A tortoise-and-snake banner with four streamers, representing the Ying-shi constellation; the streamers trail long. Formed from 㫃, with 兆 indicating the sound. The Rites of Zhou says: “Counties and border districts set up 旐.”

shuowen:4263.text: A bear banner with five streamers, representing the Fa stars; soldiers use it as a rallying signal. Formed from 㫃, with 其 indicating the sound. The Rites of Zhou says: “Those leading the du settlements set up 旗.”

shuowen:4264.text: A banner following the 旐, hanging abundantly. Formed from 㫃, with 𣎵 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4265.text: A roving chariot bears a 旌, made by attaching split feathers to the head of a yak-tail standard, to encourage the soldiers. Formed from 㫃, with 生 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4266.text: A banner of pieced leather with a bird painted on it, to encourage the troops. 旟旟 means numerous. Formed from 㫃, with 與 indicating the sound. The Rites of Zhou says: “Districts and neighborhoods set up 旟.”

shuowen:4267.text: A banner with many bells for directing the troops. Formed from 㫃, with 斤 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4268.text: What a leading chariot carries: whole feathers make its 允; 允 means advancing. Formed from 㫃, with 遂 indicating the sound. The technical term 允 is uncertain.

shuowen:4269.text: A great timber is erected with stones upon it, released by a trigger to pursue the enemy. Formed from 㫃, with 會 indicating the sound. The Spring and Autumn Commentary says: “When the 旝 moves, beat the drums.” The Odes says: “Their 旝 are like a forest.”

shuowen:4270.text: A banner with a curved handle, used to mark the troops. Formed from 㫃, with 丹 indicating the sound. The Rites of Zhou says: “A single unadorned silk cloth is 旃.”

shuowen:4271.text: A banner’s trailing streamer. Formed from 㫃, with 攸 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4272.text: A kind of banner. Formed from 㫃, with 要 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4273.text: A banner’s appearance. Formed from 㫃, with 也 indicating the sound. Luan Shi of Qi had the courtesy name Ziqi, showing that 施 means banner.

shuowen:4274.text: A banner flowing, 旖施. Formed from 㫃, with 奇 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4275.text: A banner fluttering, 旚繇. Formed from 㫃, with 票 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4276.text: The appearance of banners flying aloft. Formed from 㫃, with 猋 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4277.text: A banner’s trailing streamer. Formed from 㫃, with 汓 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4278.text: Banners bending and trailing. Formed from 㫃, with 皮 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4279.text: Turning about: signaling with banners. Formed from 㫃 and 疋; 疋 means foot.

shuowen:4280.text: A yak-tail standard. Formed from 㫃 and 毛; 毛 also indicates the sound.

shuowen:4281.text: A hanging banner, 幅胡. Formed from 㫃, with 番 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4282.text: Five hundred men of an army make a 旅. Formed from 㫃 and 从; 从 means together.

shuowen:4283.text: Arrow points, closely clustered when bundled. Formed from 㫃 and 矢.

shuowen:4284.text: Dark. Formed from 日 and 六, with 冖 indicating the sound. The count of days is ten; on the sixteenth day the moon begins to wane and darken. All characters in this group are formed from 冥.

shuowen:4285.text: Dark. Formed from 冥, with 黽 indicating the sound. Read like 黽 in 黽蛙.

shuowen:4286.text: Pure brilliance. Formed from three 日. All characters in this group are formed from 晶.

shuowen:4287.text: The essences of all things become the arrayed stars above. Formed from 晶, with 生 indicating the sound. Another explanation: pictographic, using 口; ancient 口 had a mark added inside, thus matching 日.

shuowen:4288.text: The Shang star. Formed from 晶, with 㐱 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4289.text: The Fang stars, which determine the people’s farming seasons. Formed from 晶, with 辰 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4290.text: Yang Xiong explains: ancient judicial officers decided a sentence and, after three days, carried it out once its appropriateness was established. Formed from 晶 and 宜. The fallen Xin dynasty considered three 日 in 曡 too excessive and changed them to three 田.

shuowen:4291.text: Deficient or waning: the essence of the great yin. Pictographic. All characters in this group are formed from 月.

shuowen:4292.text: The moon first revives on the first day of the month. Formed from 月, with 屰 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4293.text: The moon’s light before it becomes full. Formed from 月 and 出. The Book of Zhou says: “On bingwu, the first crescent.”

shuowen:4294.text: The moon first appearing, dimly: on the second day after a long month, the third after a short month. Formed from 月, with 䨣 indicating the sound. The Book of Zhou says: “When the lunar light first appeared.”

shuowen:4295.text: Bright. Formed from 月, with 良 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4296.text: The moon appearing in the west on the last day of the month is 朓. Formed from 月, with 兆 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4297.text: The moon appearing in the east on the first day of the month is 縮肭. Formed from 月, with 内 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4298.text: To meet. Formed from 月, with 其 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4299.text: The moon hazy, 朦朧. Formed from 月, with 蒙 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4300.text: Hazy, 朦朧. Formed from 月, with 龍 indicating the sound.
